text:
maria: Heads-up — since ~09:12 UTC a rollout of the new sidecar egress policy in eu-west1 namespace gpu-workloads has been blocking outbound traffic to gcr.io and our Prometheus pushgateway. Affected: model pulls failing, node exporters failing scrapes, many GPU jobs stuck in pull/backoff.

jake: Which pods are failing? NetworkPolicy or mesh-level egress?

maria: Mostly inference-* pods on the gpu pool and a few batch workers. It's mesh-level: Envoy logs show the egress route returning 503 + access denied. Example envoy log from one sidecar: 

```
[2026-03-18T09:13:02.123Z] "GET /v2/manifest..." 503 - "egress:policy:deny_external" source: ip-10-1-2-3 /// downstream:inbound_0
```

And `kubectl describe` on one of the pods shows the Envoy filter injected by the recent policy-rollout config: 

```
Annotations: policy.redwood.io/egress=deny-external-v2
Events:  Normal   Pulled    3m (x2 over 5m)   kubelet  Back-off pulling image
```

sam: Sounds like the new policy blocks all external hostnames unless there's a ServiceEntry (Istio) / egress mapping for them. We pushed a stricter default last night. Quick mitigation: either add ServiceEntries for gcr.io + pushgateway or patch the policy to allow those hostnames.

priya: This is causing capacity wobble — GPUs are reserved while pods retry image pulls, so cost is ticking up. We need an ETA for fix, please.

jake: I can spin a hotfix. Two options: 1) add a temporary allow-list rule in the egress policy for the known registries and metrics endpoints, or 2) annotate affected pods to bypass the policy if we trust them. Preference is (1).

maria: Agreed. Adding bypass annotations across thousands of pods is ugly. Can you push ServiceEntry + egress policy update? Hosts to allow: `gcr.io`, `storage.googleapis.com`, `pushgateway.prod.redwood-internal:9091`.

jake: Pushing a ServiceEntry and policy patch now. Patch: 

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: ServiceEntry
metadata:
  name: allow-registry-metrics
spec:
  hosts:
  - "gcr.io"
  - "storage.googleapis.com"
  - "pushgateway.prod.redwood-internal"
  ports:
  - number: 443
    name: https
    protocol: TLS
  resolution: NONE
---
apiVersion: policy.redwood.io/v1alpha1
kind: EgressPolicy
metadata:
  name: egress-exceptions-registry
spec:
  allowHosts:
  - "gcr.io"
  - "storage.googleapis.com"
  - "pushgateway.prod.redwood-internal"
  namespaces: ["gpu-workloads"]
```

sam: Nice — remember to also update the egress gateway config so NAT path doesn't get dropped. Otherwise packets will still be blocked at the gateway.

infra-bot: patch applied by jake at 2026-03-18T09:18:45Z (kubeapply job 4721). Rolling update started for gpu-workloads egress policy.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-20260318-43 created: "egress policy blocked external pulls (eu-west1)" — severity P2. Pager duty notified.

maria: Seeing successful image pulls on a couple of test pods now, and prometheus scrape for node-exporter recovered. Will watch for flaps over next 15m. Thanks @jake @sam.

priya: After stabilization, can we add a checklist item to the policy rollout playbook: "verify registry & monitoring host allowlist"? This rollout skipped that. Costs bumped ~+8% on reserved GPUs in the last hour due to retries.

maria: Good call. I'll open a follow-up doc with timeline + repro steps and tag ops-runbook.

jake: Postmortem / follow-up: revert default deny in staging until we have automated ServiceEntry generation for registries and internal telemetry endpoints.

maria: Agree — temporary mitigation applied, follow-up action items: add automated allowlist generation, update rollout checklist, run a canary in eu-west1 before global policy flips.

(End of thread)
